items.title: CoinDCX confirms $16 million loss from retired wallets days after CEO called breach reports a ‘false alarm’
items.desc: CEO Sumit Gupta had told X users on Wednesday that early reports of a breach sounded like "a false alarm."

items.title: How a DAO Vote Becomes a Treasury Transfer
items.desc: Uniswap’s executed funding proposal shows the difference between a sentiment poll, a binding vote and the contract authorized to release tokens.

items.title: How to Check a Software Wallet—and What the Checks Cannot Prove
items.desc: Fake Firefox extensions targeted recovery phrases; Electrum patched a genuine-client flaw that could trick users into signing a substituted payment.

items.title: Keystone customers say breach exposed data the hardware wallet maker promised to delete
items.desc: Keystone has said it deletes customer information 180 days after their orders in most cases, though X users have cast doubt on that claim.

items.title: ECB official sees digital euro as key to protecting EU ‘sovereignty’
items.desc: Piero Cipollone said the bloc is on track to test real transactions in 2027 and roll out a digital euro as early as 2029, pending legislation this year.

items.title: Latvia targets tokenization rules in 2027 with commercial property in focus
items.desc: Economics Minister Viktors Valainis says rules could arrive in the first half of next year, but an overdue assessment remains unfinished and no sovereign-bond issuance was identified.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Snap Two-Week Losing Streak Despite Late-Week Slide
items.desc: Spot Bitcoin ETFs finished the week with about $301 million in net inflows, ending a two-week losing streak, even as two straight days of outflows kept October in the red.

items.title: Tokenized Deposits vs. Stablecoins: What JPM Coin and USDC Holders Own
items.desc: USDC holders can transfer tokens without a Circle Mint account, but direct dollar redemption requires one. JPM Coin limits participation to approved institutional clients.

items.title: UK banks face 10,000 complaints in 3 months over crypto restrictions
items.desc: The U.K. claims to aspire to become a global cryptocurrency hub, an ambition that would appear to be at odds with the attitude to crypto purchases of its major banks.

items.title: Netanyahu floats use of blockchain as solution to potential financial sanctions
items.desc: Ahead of elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel could turn to blockchain and crypto to skirt potential international sanctions, to the dismay of opponents and the country’s central banker.

items.title: Dogecoin Foundation and House of Doge End Exclusive Brand Deal
items.desc: House of Doge keeps limited investment-product rights, while a separate deal would exchange Such App assets for $4 million in Dogecoin Labs stock.

items.title: X100 Exploit Proceeds Split Into Four 400-ETH Wallets
items.desc: The first exploiter swapped about 4.75 million USDT into ether, while the distribution wallet retained another 423 ETH.

items.title: Keystone Website Breach Exposes Customer Addresses and Order Details
items.desc: The hardware-wallet maker says it blocked access and fixed the vulnerability. Payment details, recovery phrases and private keys were not exposed, according to the company.

items.title: Electrum Patches Wallet Flaw Exploited Through Malicious Servers
items.desc: A malicious server can substitute a fake payment, then trick the user into signing it while raising the transaction fee. Developers say one user reported losing money.

items.title: Crypto longs lose $404 million in four hours as bitcoin briefly slips below $80,000
items.desc: Spot bitcoin ETFs lost $773 million on Thursday and Friday after three days of net inflows, per SoSoValue data.

items.title: ARB Touches Four-Week Low as Losses Outpace Bitcoin and Ether
items.desc: OP and POL also lost more than a quarter over matched four-week windows, while Arbitrum One's active-address count rose.

items.title: Argentine judge clears Milei and 10 others in LIBRA case, finding no ‘criminally relevant deception’
items.desc: The judge's 60-page ruling concluded Argentine President Javier Milei's post promoting the LIBRA token did not, by itself, establish fraud.

items.title: Strategy, Strive face balancing act between bitcoin buying and preferred stock dividends
items.desc: The securities have financed purchases of nearly 136,000 bitcoin, opening a funding channel that analysts expect to complement the larger ETF market.

items.title: Ether Falls Below $2,300 as 28-Day Loss Reaches 14.7%
items.desc: ETH lagged bitcoin by 9.15 percentage points over matched nearly four-week windows, while US ether ETFs recorded another outflow on Oct. 22.

items.title: Third X100 Exploit Transaction Pulls 550,000 X From Uniswap Pool
items.desc: A different sender routed about 549,916 X and 1,909 USDT to a new beneficiary, while the affected pool held less than 200 USDT.

items.title: Crypto under weekend pressure, bitcoin slides below $80,000 on U.S. Middle East evacuations
items.desc: Bitcoin has sunk to its weakest level in more than one month.

items.title: Game Publishers Have Pushed to Cut Discs Since 2007, Infinity Ward Veteran Says
items.desc: Robert Bowling, who spent six years working on Call of Duty, told Decrypt that Activision suggested cutting discs nearly two decades ago.

items.title: X100 Exploit Nets 4.85 Million USDT After Governance Takeover
items.desc: Two transactions turned treasury tokens and liquidity positions into USDT; Blockaid warned that the Ethereum attack was ongoing.

items.title: Argentina drops criminal probe into President Milei over crashed memecoin LIBRA
items.desc: The judge found that Milei's promotion of LIBRA did not constitute fraud, despite the attention his support drew to the token.

items.title: Shaw Publishes Daos.fun Reconstruction, Claims Critical Flaw
items.desc: The repository reports matching captured and rebuilt binaries. Daos.fun says it no longer maintains the platform, though existing tokens remain tradable.

items.title: Hyperliquid’s Yan and CME’s Duffy Split Over Who Must Bear US Compliance
items.desc: Yan favors oversight of market deployers rather than the blockchain, while Hyperliquid’s interface still bars US-based users and VPN circumvention.

items.title: Wells Fargo, Cisco, Marvell among latest firms objecting to OKXICE's tokenized stock plan
items.desc: Six more companies have objected to listing tokenized versions of their stock on the venue, Reuters reported, bringing the total to 22.

items.title: Bitcoin’s wealthy holders turning to loans and yield as investment habits mature: Xapo CEO
items.desc: Borrowing against bitcoin and earning income to build their BTC holdings are becoming priorities for long-term investors, Xapo Bank CEO Seamus Rocca told CoinDesk.

items.title: API Key Rotation: What Revocation and Redeployment Actually Change
items.desc: Scheduled replacement can let two keys overlap. Suspected exposure makes that overlap a security decision, not just a way to avoid downtime.

items.title: Hong Kong’s Biggest Bank Puts a Stablecoin in 3 Million Wallets
items.desc: HSBC switched on its Hong Kong dollar stablecoin inside PayMe on Friday, testing whether a bank-issued token can become everyday money.

items.title: U.S. Clarity Act failure gives Asia and Middle East a competitive edge, says Apex Group CEO
items.desc: Apex Group CEO Peter Hughes warned that the failure of the U.S. Clarity Act will drive digital asset businesses toward faster-moving jurisdictions in Asia and the Middle East.

items.title: Arthur Hayes Says He Sold Maelstrom’s Directional Book
items.desc: Hayes-linked wallets transferred 8,000 ETH and six other tokens, contrasting with his Oct. 15 declaration that he was long Bitcoin and Ether.

items.title: Franklin Templeton adds $150 million in fund shares to XRP Ledger, all in one wallet
items.desc: Two subscriptions on Thursday nearly quadrupled the fund’s tokens on the network. The receiving wallet shares its authorized signers with the issuer.

items.title: Kraken Scraps Monero Withdrawal Questionnaires, Keeps XMR Listed
items.desc: Source-of-funds checks remain, but co-CEO Arjun Sethi says asking what clients will do with withdrawn coins is unacceptable.

items.title: Sezzle Pursues National Bank Charter to Add FDIC-Insured Deposit Accounts
items.desc: FinTech company Sezzle has begun the formal charter application process to establish a national bank that would offer a broad range of banking products and services, the company said in a Thursday (Oct. 22) press release.
